summary:
Tiny Habitat is a browser-based educational game where children aged 7–12 manage a Mars outpost for ten Martian days, or sols. Players select cargo within a weight limit and make decisions that balance life support, power and radiation shielding. Their robot companion, Robo, explains each choice’s consequences, turning resource management into understandable science lessons.

NASA’s DONKI API supplies recorded solar observations that influence the mission’s solar encounter. Real NASA photographs and sourced facts appear automatically and are collected in a Mission Album. Mini-games add hands-on activities, while classroom mode, printable lessons, discussion questions and certificates help teachers extend the experience.

Saved observations and written summary fallbacks support play when external services fail. Through meaningful choices and gentle opportunities to retry, Tiny Habitat makes space science approachable and engaging—delivering knowledge through fun.
details:
Tiny Habitat is an interactive, browser-based educational game designed to teach children aged 7–12 about space exploration by having them manage a simulated Mars outpost over ten Martian days (sols).
​Players begin by packing cargo within strict weight limits and then make daily operational decisions balancing life support, power management, and radiation shielding. Real NASA data—such as solar observations fetched via the DONKI API—directly impacts the gameplay, triggering dynamic solar encounters. As players progress, they unlock real NASA photographs and verified facts, which are collected in a digital Mission Album. A built-in robot companion, Robo, provides contextual feedback on the scientific consequences of their choices.
​The project was developed using a modern web stack. The frontend is built with React, TypeScript, Vite, and Tailwind CSS to ensure a responsive, kid-friendly user interface. The backend is powered by Python using FastAPI and Flask to handle data routing and API integrations.
​By translating complex resource management and real space weather data into a manageable, fun format, this project aims to make NASA's open data approachable. It empowers educators through classroom modes and printable lessons, ultimately inspiring the next generation of junior astronauts.
